improved: When ERA's endpoint is busy or not answering, a page says so and asks you to try again shortly, instead of waiting for a time-out.
The Export menu says when a resource has more than 5,000 properties: the export then holds the first 5,000, always the same ones.
Links in ERA's data open only when they are web addresses, and links to other sites don't pass on the page you came from.
With reduced motion switched on in your system, transitions and animations end at once.
fixed: The sitemaps no longer time out: they are built in the background once a day.

new: Every infrastructure element has a page now, not only sections of line and tracks: operational points, tunnels, platforms, sidings, signals and the rest get their map, identification, country, validity and parts.

A RINF parameters tab lists every parameter of a resource in the order of the RINF index, grouped by chapter, with a filter. It includes the parameters of a track's contact line system, ETCS and train detection systems, and those marked not applicable or not yet available.

Operational points have their own page: the sections of line that meet there as spokes pointing the way they leave, a schematic of the tracks with their platforms and sidings, tables of tracks, platforms and sidings, and what the tracks allow (speed, gauge, energy, ETCS, train length).
Platform edges show a side view of their height against the TSI heights of 550 and 760 mm, and their usable length against regional and long-distance trains.
Sidings show their usable length against passenger and freight trains, their servicing facilities and the energy they offer.
Tunnels show their length, fire category, safety installations and documents.

National lines have a page: the line on the map, a profile along km with the speed, energy supply, ETCS, gauge and number of tracks of each section, its sections and operational points in km order, and its kilometric posts.

Sections of line show what lies along them at its km: tunnels, phase separations and kilometric posts. They list their neighbouring sections and their restrictions (axle load, load capability, noise, operational regime, industrial risk).
Tracks show a cross-section on the Route compatibility tab (gauge, gauging profile, contact wire height, rail inclination), the platforms along them, and their running direction as an arrow.
Contact line systems, ETCS installations and train detection systems have their own page, with the tracks that use them. The energy supply shows as a symbol in OpenRailwayMap's colours.
Infrastructure managers show key figures: operational points, sections of line, km of line, tracks, and the shares of energy supply and ETCS level. These pages are kept for a day.

Primary locations show their code, country, region, use (passenger, freight, container handling, handover point), the operational points and subsidiary locations that refer to them, and flags that change over time.
Signals show their type, ID, orientation as an arrow, distance to the danger point and km.
Reference border points show the two countries and the operational points on either side, on the map too.
Kilometric posts, hot axle box detectors, bridges, TEN-T classifications, documents and linear elements (with the elements they connect to) have pages of their own.
Every signal, switch, level crossing and other point asset shows the national line and km it is at.

A Data model tab draws UML class diagrams from ERA's own SHACL shapes. "What this page shows" follows every value on the page back through the model, however many links away, and names the rows that show each property; the class view lists all attributes of the class and its superclasses and marks what this resource has.

RINF code lists have pages: a concept scheme shows its concepts as a tree with a filter and the ERA properties that use it; a concept shows its branch of the scheme, marked, with its broader, narrower, related and matching concepts.
Linear elements show their net relations two steps out as a graph, placed as on the map, with arrows the way a train can pass, and what is positioned on them along their length and by type.
Kilometric posts show their linear element and offset, and their place on the line between its operational points and the next posts.
Reference border points list the operational points that name them or are placed on them, their primary locations and the sections of line at the border.
An RDF tab shows a resource's triples as Turtle, RDF/XML, JSON-LD or N-Triples, highlighted, with every IRI linking to its page; copy or download them. The exports add RDF/XML and JSON-LD.

The data model diagram zooms (Ctrl+scroll, pinch or buttons), pans by dragging and opens full screen. A content tree shows either view as a tree whose links open into the class they point at, and the diagram exports as SVG, PlantUML or Mermaid.
National line profiles add lanes for class B, gauging profile, axle load and gradient (the steepest gradient per km).

Infrastructure managers' shares are by track-km of their sections of line rather than by number of tracks, and add track gauge and gauging profile. Infrabel's electrified share now reads 91% of line track-km.
improved: Every page is now built on the spot from ERA's SPARQL endpoint, so it always shows what ERA publishes today. The notes about the describe index are gone.
The search box finds names through RINF Atlas's search; a pasted IRI still opens directly.
Hover a parameter's name for its definition and RINF index from ERA's ontology; units come from the ontology too.
The country shows its flag, and dates with a time zone show the right day.
Maps can show more than the resource: an operational point's sections of line are a layer you can switch off, and clicking a line opens its page.
Long tables show the first 100 rows and a Show more button.
Documents without a name are named after their document id instead of 'download'.
Pages of national lines are kept for a day, since they sum up all their sections and tracks.
A resource published by several providers opens in the provider whose code it carries.
Map layers can hold points as well as lines: click a dot to open it.
Operational point connections point each spoke to the far end of its section; a spoke opens its section, and a table lists the sections.
A section of line's route diagram runs from hub to hub.
An open-ended validity period puts today in the middle of its time axis.
Incoming links show "Linked from" before the property.
A resource typed in several graphs is read from the graph that says most about it after the provider's own, so SKOS concepts copied into provider graphs show in full.
fixed: The tab bar no longer shows a small vertical scroll bar.

new: Resources that are not in the index yet get their full page, built live from ERA's SPARQL endpoint in about a tenth of a second: route, map, track summaries, tables and data status, the same as an indexed page.
improved: All properties and Incoming links show their counts on pages read live too, and "read live from ERA" under the title says where a page comes from.

new: Section of line pages show the train protection legacy system of their tracks.
improved: The national line of a section of line links to the line's own page.
ETCS and the train protection legacy system are also read from the common characteristics subsets a track belongs to, so tracks that only state them there show them too.
fixed: Operational points, national lines and tracks show their name instead of their address in the tracks table, All properties, Incoming links and the graph.

new: Pages for sections of line: route diagram with km positions, map, the parameters of their tracks summed up, a table of the tracks and the validity period.
Pages for running tracks: an Overview with the gradient profile, contact line and ETCS, and a Route compatibility tab.
All properties, Incoming links and Graph for every resource, and exports as Turtle, N-Triples or CSV.
Resources outside the index are read live from ERA.
Share copies a link to the page you are on, including its tab; on a phone it opens the share sheet.
Help, a short tour on the first visit, an About dialog and this list of changes.
